source: Roark's Formulas, Table 8.1 case 1a (cantilever, end load), with shear
request:
Plan: 200 x 10 x 20 mm mild steel (S235) bar, clamped at the wall end, loaded at the free end by the weight of 50 kg = 50 x 9.81 = 490.5 N straight down (bar is 20 mm tall in Z, so it bends about the weak-looking but stated 10 x 20 section with the 20 mm side vertical). Self-weight of the bar is ignored. The result is checked against the cantilever hand calculation.


source: custom shape: a valid printable solid; fit judged by eye
request:
Plan: custom clip, PETG, FDM (my defaults). Three open-top channels of 6.4 mm diameter (0.4 mm clearance on a 6 mm cable) at 8.4 mm pitch with 2 mm walls, each with a 4.8 mm snap-in slit so cables press in. A 3 mm thick mounting ear (14 mm long) carries one 4.5 mm clearance hole for the M4 screw. Flat mounting face on z = 0 goes against the desk underside; slits open on the +Z side, away from the desk.

```python
from build123d import *
from engagent.cad import params, save
P = params(d=6.4, wall=2.0, slit=4.8, height=14.0, width=16.0, ear_len=14.0, ear_t=3.0, screw_hole=4.5)
n_pitch = P.d + P.wall
length = 3 * P.d + 4 * P.wall
zc = 6.0   # cable axis height above the desk face

body = Box(length, P.width, P.height, align=(Align.MIN, Align.MIN, Align.MIN))
ear = Pos(-P.ear_len, 0, 0) * Box(P.ear_len + 1.0, P.width, P.ear_t, align=(Align.MIN, Align.MIN, Align.MIN))
part = body + ear

for i in range(3):
    cx = P.wall + P.d / 2 + i * n_pitch
    part -= Pos(cx, P.width / 2, zc) * Rot(90, 0, 0) * Cylinder(P.d / 2, P.width * 3)
    slit_h = P.height + 2.0 - zc
    part -= Pos(cx, P.width / 2, zc + slit_h / 2) * Box(P.slit, P.width * 3, slit_h)

part -= Pos(-P.ear_len / 2, P.width / 2, 0) * Cylinder(P.screw_hole / 2, P.height * 3)
save(part)
```
```bash
ea make geometry.py --print petg --name "cable clip"
```

source: Lame thick-walled cylinder, open ends (axial stress 0): von Mises at the bore
request:
Plan: steel tube 100 mm OD, 60 mm bore, 200 mm long, 100 MPa internal pressure, open ends (no axial pressure load on the ends). No tube-with-bore template for a full round tube, so a custom script; I model one quarter with symmetry planes (x = 0, y = 0 and the z = 0 end slide on their own plane only), which leaves the tube free to expand. Pressure on the bore. Checked against the Lame thick-wall solution (peak von Mises at the bore).

```python
from build123d import *
from engagent.cad import params, save
P = params(od=100.0, bore=60.0, length=200.0)
tube = Cylinder(P.od / 2, P.length, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
tube -= Pos(0, 0, P.length / 2) * Cylinder(P.bore / 2, P.length * 3)
quarter = Box(P.od / 2, P.od / 2, P.length, align=(Align.MIN, Align.MIN, Align.MIN))
part = tube & quarter
save(part)
```
```bash
ea make geometry.py --name "tube quarter model"
ea analyze last -m steel_generic --slide xmin x --slide ymin y --slide zmin z --pressure hole:60 100 --check "cylinder.lame_thick ri=30 ro=50 p=100 -> stress@max_von_mises"
```

Plan: custom comb, PETG, FDM (my defaults). Plate 60 x 20 x 5 mm (long edge along X), five 4 mm wide slots cut in from the long edge at y = 20, each 12 mm deep, evenly spaced (about 6.7 mm of tooth between slots and at the ends).

```python
from build123d import *
from engagent.cad import params, save
P = params(length=60.0, width=20.0, thickness=5.0, slot=4.0, depth=12.0)
part = Box(P.length, P.width, P.thickness, align=(Align.MIN, Align.MIN, Align.MIN))
gap = (P.length - 5 * P.slot) / 6
for i in range(5):
    cx = gap + P.slot / 2 + i * (P.slot + gap)
    cut_len = P.depth + 2.0
    part -= Pos(cx, P.width - P.depth + cut_len / 2, P.thickness / 2) * Box(P.slot, cut_len, P.thickness * 3)
save(part)
```
```bash
ea make geometry.py --print petg --name "cable comb"
```

source: dimensions as asked; D-shaft 6 mm with 4.5 mm flat
request:
Plan: custom knob, PETG, FDM (my defaults). Round knob 30 mm diameter x 15 mm tall, top edge rounded 1.5 mm. D-shaped blind hole in the bottom: 6 mm circle with the flat cut so the hole is 4.5 mm across the flat, 10 mm deep (leaves 5 mm closed on top). Print it top-down on the bed; the D hole is exactly 6 mm as stated, with no extra clearance added.

```python
from build123d import *
from engagent.cad import params, save
P = params(diameter=30.0, height=15.0, shaft=6.0, across=4.5, depth=10.0)
knob = Pos(P.diameter / 2, P.diameter / 2, 0) * Cylinder(P.diameter / 2, P.height, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
knob = fillet(knob.edges().group_by(Axis.Z)[-1], 1.5)
dcut = Cylinder(P.shaft / 2, P.depth + 1.0, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
dcut &= Pos(-P.shaft / 2 + P.across / 2, 0, 0) * Box(P.across, P.shaft * 2, P.depth + 1.0, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
part = knob - Pos(P.diameter / 2, P.diameter / 2, -1.0) * dcut
save(part)
```
```bash
ea make geometry.py --print petg --name "D-shaft knob"
```
